note: Image-drawn annotations for the M4 Part B assisted mask-to-cell control. Every point below was picked by looking at the screenshot itself - the repeating nested-square decorative motif on the interior walls, assumed one motif per block face (a standard per-block decorative texture convention) - not read from cameras.json, the reference litematic, or any F3 text visible in the frame. That assumption is stated, not hidden: it is exactly the kind of thing a real user would also be estimating by eye, and the block count on each frame is a best-effort visual count, not a precise measurement. `visible_extent_polygon` is a rough quadrilateral around the chosen wall itself, drawn by eye - using 'everything not occluded' as the mask (an earlier version of this file) fed plane_window regions showing entirely different, near-grazing-incidence surfaces (ceiling, opposite wall) for this axis and blew up its window computation (span ~283145, block_px ~0.003). The extent polygon is the fix: it scopes the mask to the plane actually being measured, and occlusion regions are subtracted from inside it.
